claims: The RFB key injector unpaused the container headlessly (Space toggled status 1->0).
Live PINE diffs found words that respond to the arrow keys.
0x241b60 reads (5,4,4) across slots 102/103/104, so it is not a per-car highlight id.
The menu highlight is not stored as a per-car integer in EE.
args.evidence: Mark-number live attempt, headless: unpaused the container via a stdlib RFB key injector to the container's own Xvfb (no host focus); live PINE diff found words that respond to the arrow keys (0x241b60, 0x241e00 change with L/J but not without input). DECISIVE TEST: loaded slots 102/103/104 (highlights car1/car5/car4 = positions 1/5/4) live and read the candidates: 0x241b60 reads (5,4,4) and 0x241e00 reads (5,4,4) - NOT a per-car id (car5 and car4 both read 4). So the responsive words are an animation/other cursor, NOT the mark. Combined with the exhaustive scan (no width holds (1,5,4)), the conclusion stands: the menu highlight is not stored as a per-car integer in EE. The live method itself works (keys + PINE reads headless).
